subject: Decision Making
title: Bernoulli and Expected Utility
description: A short lesson to help you apply Bernoulli and Expected Utility.

hook.text: Daniel Bernoulli noticed that a dollar means more to a poor person than a rich one. Obvious, but no one had proved it.

buildup.text: He proposed that people do not maximize money. They maximize utility, a subjective sense of satisfaction.

discovery.text: This explained risk aversion. Losing $100 hurts more than gaining $100 feels good because utility curves flatten.

twist.text: Bernoulli published in 1738. Economists ignored him for 200 years until von Neumann revived the idea.

climax.text: Expected utility is now the foundation of economics. Every model of rational choice traces back to Bernoulli.

punchline.text: A dollar is not a dollar. Bernoulli proved that value is subjective.

quiz.question: What did Bernoulli's expected utility theory explain?
options: Why losing $100 hurts more than gaining $100 feels good
